desc:
A grid grid holds small non-negative integers (think of colours). Find the largest axis-aligned rectangle of consecutive rows and columns in which all cells have the same value, and return its area (number of cells). Any value may be used, but all cells of the rectangle must share it.

Example: [[1,1,2],[1,1,2],[3,2,2]] returns 4 (the 2 by 2 block of ones; the twos form an L-shaped region whose largest rectangle has only 2 cells... the column of twos in the top two rows).
constraints: All rows have the same length
hints: For a single value this is the maximal rectangle of ones problem. You could run it once per value, but the values may be many. Can one sweep handle all of them?
For each cell keep up[r][c]: how many cells directly above it (including itself) have the same value as the cell. This is the histogram height for a rectangle whose bottom edge is on row r.

In row r a rectangle can only use adjacent columns that hold the same value in that row. Split the row into runs of equal values and solve the histogram stack separately inside each run, using up[r][c] as the bar heights.
editorial: Let up[r][c] be the length of the vertical run of equal values ending at (r, c): up[r][c] = up[r-1][c] + 1 if grid[r][c] == grid[r-1][c], else 1. A uniform rectangle whose bottom row is r and whose columns are c1..c2 needs grid[r][c1] == ... == grid[r][c2], and its height can be at most min(up[r][c1..c2]) because each column's cells above must equal the bottom cell. Because the bottom cells are equal, all the cells of the rectangle share one value.

So for each row cut the columns into maximal runs of equal values and run the largest-rectangle-in-histogram stack on up[r][c] within each run. Take the maximum area over all rows and runs. Every cell is handled a constant number of times: O(R * C) time and O(C) extra space. A grid with one value reduces to the plain full rectangle R * C.
solution:
def largestUniformRectangle(grid):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    up = [0] * cols
    prev = [None] * cols
    best = 0
    for r in range(rows):
        row = grid[r]
        for c in range(cols):
            up[c] = up[c] + 1 if prev[c] == row[c] else 1
        prev = row
        c = 0
        while c < cols:
            e = c
            while e + 1 < cols and row[e + 1] == row[c]:
                e += 1
            # largest rectangle in histogram up[c..e]
            stack = []
            for i in range(c, e + 2):
                h = up[i] if i <= e else 0
                start = i
                while stack and stack[-1][1] >= h:
                    s, sh = stack.pop()
                    best = max(best, sh * (i - s))
                    start = s
                stack.append((start, h))
            c = e + 1
    return best
